pack.title: Profanity Reviewer Knowledge Pack
pack.purpose: Provide reviewer knowledge for direct profanity and abusive speech under the existing V2 profanity policy.
protected_interests: clear distinction between direct use and contextual mention
required_evidence: An admissible chunk-level evidence span containing a literal profanity term or phrase.
A direct utterance, narration, or quoted span that contains the profane wording itself.
insufficient_evidence: A neutral mention that a profanity term exists without the term being used as speech.
An inferential claim that relies on context but does not preserve literal chunk evidence.
A fragmented or indirect reference with no actual profanity phrase in the chunk.
reviewer_heuristics: Literal profanity is the strongest signal and should be treated as a direct hit when admissible.
Quotation, education, and condemnation can change the interpretation enough to suppress a violation.
Dialogue and narration can still be direct profanity if the literal wording is present.
The reviewer should anchor the finding to the exact literal phrase, not the surrounding narrative alone.
positive_examples: Direct profanity: يا كلب — Direct insult.
Profanity in narration: كان يصرخ: يا حمار — Direct insult.
Profanity insult with explicit term: يا خرا — Direct insult.
Profanity with direct address: يا نصاب — Direct insult.
Profanity with abusive phrase: العن أمك — Severe abusive phrase.
negative_examples: Quoted profanity: المعلم قال: "يا كلب" — The teacher is reporting a quoted sentence.
Educational profanity discussion: في الدرس نشرح معنى كلمة يا حمار — The scene is instructional and explanatory.
Condemned profanity: الشخصية تدين قول يا خرا وتصفه بالإهانة — The story rejects abusive language.
Dictionary reference to profanity: في القاموس توجد كلمة سباب ضمن الأمثلة — This is a lexical explanation, not a use of profanity.
Neutral mention of profanity term: المشهد يذكر كلمة شتيمة فقط — No endorsement or direct insult appears.
common_false_positives: Quoted profanity presented as a quotation rather than a direct insult.
Educational discussion of a profanity term without endorsement.
Condemnation of the profanity word or phrase.
Neutral narration that merely references the concept without the literal profanity text.

glossary_relationships.note: The term is a lexical trigger for the profanity concept.
The term maps directly to the profanity concept.
The term is treated as a profanity-related lexical anchor.

article_mapping.note: Current V2 profanity implementation routes to article 4.
The same profanity payload can affect age classification.
Direct profanity can also implicate dignity and reputation.

reporting_guidance: Report the exact literal profanity phrase and the immediate context used to interpret it.
Use the selected article mapping to explain the policy basis of the finding.
If the context is quotation, educational discussion, or condemnation, suppress the finding or mark it for review according to the module outcome.
